findings.text: The step declared outside machine replay ("that the 18 constraint polynomials are the entries of the stated matrix equation and the objective is the stated functional") cites tests/test_p3_moment.py as pinning, but no run record, hash, or evidence entry for that test file appears anywhere in the ledger record; within the record this step rests solely on the readable `about` formulas. I re-derived all 18 entries against them: constraints[0],[1] are |a|^2-1, |b|^2-1; Re E_00/E_11/E_22/E_33 carry the Bell diagonal 1/2 weights (e.g. constraints[2] has "11":-1/2,"12":-1/2 for phi+-, constraints[3] has "13":-1/2,"14":-1/2 for psi+-); Re/Im E_03 and E_12 carry the off-diagonal +-1/2 Bell entries (constraints[10]: "11":-1/2,"12":1/2; constraints[12]: "13":-1/2,"14":1/2); sA a0 conj(a1) appears exactly in E_02/E_13 and sB b0 conj(b1) in E_01/E_23; the W terms are the row Gram products with indices matching the `variables` list; `objective` {"8":-1,"9":-1,"10":-4,"11".."14":1} with bound "0" is exactly the stated inequality. The disclosed verification boundary is therefore honest, but its cited test pinning is unverifiable from the record. [claims/evidence/p3_moment/one_body_usd_lemma.json, about.verification_boundary (phrase "pinned by tests/test_p3_moment.py") vs constraints/objective/variables fields]

The first PASS entry records "argv=None cwd=None exit=None env_sha256=None" -- a recorded verdict with no execution provenance (not even an exit status). The charter's replay requirement is carried entirely by the 02:41:39 reverify entry, whose structured details (gram_dim 128, n_constraints 18, bound "0", failure "") match the file's 128-element gram_basis, 18 constraints and 18 multipliers, and bound field, under the same binary_hash 68a61a8d... that the certification record stamps. [Evidence entry 2026-10-27T02:11:17+00:00, note field "argv=None cwd=None exit=None env_sha256=None"]

The prose "tr(Y D) = (sA + sB)|a|^2|b|^2 + 2c(|a|^2 + |b|^2)" uses a symbol D defined nowhere in the file (only E and W are named in about.constraints); from its stated value D must denote the three one-body terms of E. All quantitative cross-checks pass: multipliers[0] = -2c + sum(lam)/2 - (sA+sB)|b|^2 and multipliers[1] = -2c + sum(lam)/2 - (sA+sB) match the prose "-(sA+sB)|b|^2 - 2c + sum(lam)/2 and -(sA+sB) - 2c + sum(lam)/2 on the two norm constraints"; multipliers[2] {"2,2":1,"3,3":1,"6,6":1,"7,7":1} equals Y_00 = |a1|^2 + |b1|^2 as "Y's entries on E's entries" requires; the JSON `statement` field is byte-identical to the ledger statement, as the Notes assert. [claims/evidence/p3_moment/one_body_usd_lemma.json, about.proof_inside_the_certificate (phrase "tr(Y D)")]

Notes record "statement corrected after review round 1" (removal of an attainment clause is a semantic change), yet formulation_version still reads "p3-sos-certificate-v1" with no amendment marker, so the record alone cannot determine which statement text any round-1 artifacts were bound to under this id/version pair. The current promotion is nonetheless unambiguous: the receipt binds to the verbatim statement, and the single evidence file (sha256 4dcad293...) contains that exact text, so CONJECTURED was re-earned on the corrected text by both PASS replays. [Notes phrase "statement corrected after review round 1" vs formulation_version field "p3-sos-certificate-v1"]

The golden suite listing "sos-2 -> FAIL, sos-3 -> FAIL, sos-4 -> FAIL" carries no expected-verdict labels; that these are expected negative cases follows only from the stamping rule ("stamps only when every golden case yields its expected verdict") combined with the 2026-10-27T02:11:09 stamp and the matching binary_hash/golden_suite_hash. Remaining ledger checks: dependencies "(none)" makes the level-cap rule vacuous; CONJECTURED -> CERTIFIED matches level semantics (replayed PASS plus this review receipt); CONJECTURED's "not yet reviewed" is consistent with round 1 having reviewed the pre-correction text. [Verifier declaration, golden suite listing for sos_certificate v1.0, and Dependencies field "(none)"]

Hypothesis inventory is complete; no hidden assumption found. "unit vectors a, b" <-> constraints[0],[1]; "real numbers s_A, s_B, c" and "real numbers lambda_B" <-> real variables 8-14; "for some complex 4x4 matrix W" <-> 32 free real variables 15-46; the tensor-order convention (first factor carries |a><a| (x) I, index 2j+k) is disclosed in about.variables; about.statement_note correctly records that no sign hypotheses on s_A, s_B, c, lambda_B are used and that the W W^dagger form is equivalent to positive semidefiniteness, so the statement text omits no scope word the certificate relies on. [Statement phrases "unit vectors", "real numbers", "for some complex 4x4 matrix W" vs about.statement_note, about.variables, constraints[0]-[1]]

The title phrase inside the bound text ("One-body unambiguous-discrimination lemma") embeds an operational interpretation that the certificate does not establish; what is machine-replayed (exact-rational identity bound - objective - sum(multiplier*constraint) = b^T Q b with Q PSD on the 128-monomial basis, PASS twice) plus the disclosed encoding step yields exactly the inequality after the colon -- the correct content for CERTIFIED within the disclosed boundary. The weak-duality argument is sound (Y PSD always, <B|Y|B> = 1 at unit norm, tr(Y c I) = 4c explains the "4c"), and the round-1 removal of the "unsupported attainment clause" eliminated the one prior overclaim; the requested level does not exceed the evidence. [Statement prefix "One-body unambiguous-discrimination lemma (two qubits):" vs about.verification_boundary]

Ordering and preconditions check out: the verifier was certified at 2026-10-27T02:11:09, eight seconds before the first replay at 02:11:17, so both PASSes are replays by an already-certified verifier; the reverify at 02:41:39 adds matching structured output; the round-1 defect named in Notes ("an unsupported attainment clause") is absent from the current conclusion, which is the bare inequality; with no dependencies and a disclosed, reviewer-checked boundary, nothing further gates promoting now. The tight certify-then-replay interval within one pipeline session is the only timing observation, and the independence this receipt supplies is what the CERTIFIED level requires. [Certification record timestamp 2026-10-27T02:11:09 vs evidence timestamps 02:11:17 and 02:41:39]
